artists.biography: Antimatter, a UK dark rock band, is the solo project of longtime founding member Mick Moss. The project was originally a duo composed of founding member Duncan Patterson (former bassist/songwriter of Anathema) and Moss, being essentially an amalgamation of two solo projects working in tandem with each other, with each member writing and arranging their songs alone and compiling them in the studio later on to create an album. In this manner the pair released three albums together, Saviour, Lights Out and Planetary Confinement, after which Patterson left, in 2005, to start another band Íon. Moss continued Antimatter as an extension of his own timeline established throughout the first three discs, releasing the project's fourth album Leaving Eden in 2007. Moss followed with 'Live@An Club', (released on his own label Music in Stone), Alternative Matter, Fear of a Unique Identity, The Judas Table, "Too Late", Welcome To The Machine, Live Between The Earth & Clouds, and, most recently, Black Market Enlightenment in 2018.[

perplexity.description:
The Judas Table, released on 9 October 2015, is the sixth studio album by the UK band Antimatter, issued through Prophecy Productions. Musically, it blends progressive rock and hard rock elements, showcasing a dark, atmospheric sound marked by introspective lyrics and layered instrumentation. Mick Moss, the band's principal songwriter and vocalist, leads the album with a mix of electric and acoustic guitars, keyboards, and emotive vocals, supported by guest musicians on bass, violin, additional vocals, and drums.

Positioned in Antimatter's discography as a mature and refined work, The Judas Table has been critically acclaimed for its depth and cohesiveness. It was notably voted the number 1 "Album of the Decade" (2010s) by Dead Rhetoric's David E. Gehlke and ranked among the "Top 25 Progressive Metal Albums Of The Decade" by Dutch Progressive Rock Page's Andy Read, reflecting its strong reception within progressive and metal circles. The album's themes often explore betrayal and personal struggle, delivered through a somber yet powerful musical approach that solidified its status as a significant release in the band's career.
